title: Consolidated animal post-mortem reference data
purpose: Normalize the animal names in the supplied project data and apply the available general guidance to each animal with its source and inference status preserved.
importantInterpretation: General ranges below are educational reference values, not validated species-specific post-mortem intervals. Normal live-animal temperature is not a measured temperature at death. Do not derive a species-specific time of death from these ranges alone.

normalization: Cow and cattle are one cattle record.
Chicken and poultry are one chicken record; chicken measurements do not represent every bird species.
Giraffe / hanging animal is a giraffe record; hanging animal describes posture, not a species.
Camel is included because it is an application species, although it has no species record in deathp1.json, deathp2.json, or deathp3.json.
animalInventory.emptyInput: deathwithlongname.json is empty (0 bytes) and contributes no animal records.

project_p1.claims: Species normal-temperature entries and general rigor, cooling-rate, lecture cooling-guide, and size-group equilibration entries; source locations are recorded in the source text in that file.

project_p2.claims: General livor appearance and fixation ranges, movement and contact modifiers, and animal-specific posture or pigmentation notes.

project_p3.claims: Byte-for-byte duplicate of deathp1.json; treated as a repeated extraction, not independent confirmation.

merck_normal_rectal_temperature.title: Normal Rectal Temperature Ranges
merck_normal_rectal_temperature.claims: Normal rectal temperature ranges for common domestic animals, including cattle, horse, sheep, goat, pig, dog, cat, rabbit, and daylight chicken.

fao_animal_body.kind: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations reference chapter
fao_animal_body.title: Chapter 2: The animal body, Unit 4: Body temperature
fao_animal_body.claims: General live-animal temperature references, including camel; explains camel temperature variation with time of day and water availability.

giraffe_field_immobilisation.title: Effective Field Immobilisation and Capture of Giraffe (Giraffa camelopardalis)
giraffe_field_immobilisation.claims: Reports an adult giraffe normal body-temperature guide of 37–38.6 °C in a field-immobilisation context.

giraffe_translocation_manual.title: A Journey of Giraffe: A Practical Guide to Wild Giraffe Translocations
giraffe_translocation_manual.claims: Gives a giraffe body-temperature guide of 38.5 ± 0.5 °C in an operational translocation context.

deer_temperature_study.title: Comparison of tympanic membrane and rectal temperatures of anesthetized fallow deer (Dama dama)
deer_temperature_study.claims: Reports rectal temperatures measured during recovery from anesthesia; this is not a normal baseline range and is retained only as context.

wildlife_forensics_handbook.title: Handbook on Standard Operating Procedures in Forensic Investigations of Suspected Illegal Killing of Wildlife
wildlife_forensics_handbook.claims: Post-mortem changes depend on species, size, activity, cause of death, and environment; cooling is slower in large insulated mammals than in emaciated birds; animal-specific data are limited and human cooling models should not simply be extrapolated to animal species.

generalDefaults.status: General guidance inherited by every species record below; no claim is species-validated unless a species-specific source is explicitly listed.

coolingRateCPerHour.source: deathp1.json, unspecified.algor.rateCPerHour; death p1.pdf, PDF p. 15

globalLimitations: Species and size are only two of many influences on post-mortem changes; activity before death, cause of death, ambient temperature and moisture, sun, rain, insulation, fat, airflow, surface contact, hydration, age, and body condition also matter.
The supplied project files contain no known-time-of-death test cases for the listed species.
Species-specific postmortem rates are not inferred from live-animal temperature ranges.
The size-based equilibration assignments are assumptions based on typical adult animals; use actual body mass and insulation when known.
deathp3.json duplicates deathp1.json and does not provide independent replication.
